body: Writing uses recurring marks and conventions to represent language. Some records begin with practical information about quantities or people. The Metropolitan Museum of Art interprets the clay tablet in the image library as a probable account of barley and emmer wheat. Its material helps it survive, and understanding the marks still depends on comparing many records.

Other writing traditions left different materials and purposes. At Yin Xu in China, inscriptions on oracle bones are evidence of writing in the late Shang period. Written documents can preserve evidence of transactions, names or speech. Surviving documents reflect particular authors, institutions and conditions of preservation.

limitations: The oldest surviving evidence of a practice may be younger than the practice itself. Written records preserve only part of what people communicated.
purpose: Distinguish durable records of language from spoken and signed communication.
